$comment: GM LS1 5.7 L Gen III small-block V8 (launch swap). Researched 2026-09-29. Primary sources: GM Heritage Center vehicle information kits on gm.com (1997 Corvette with GM Powertrain engine sheets; 1998 and 1999 Camaro with the AAMA/MVMA specification forms; 2000, 2001 and 2004 Corvette and 2002 Camaro restoration kits), read from page images; GM service information for the 1998-2004 Corvette as reproduced by Mitchell Repair (archive.org, text layer); Holden owner's handbooks (archive.org copy of Holden's own PDFs) and Holden VT II and VZ Monaro brochures; Pontiac GTO and Trans Am brochures. Swap hardware (bellhousing, flexplates, pans, dimensions, reported limits) is from Speedway Motors tech articles, Holley's 302-1/302-2 instruction sheet and parts retailers. Dry weight is GM's MVMA dressed-engine figure (F-body). Outline dimensions are a vendor figure (single source). GM publishes no injector flow, cam duration or outline dimensions for the LS1. Some GM documents disagree on the 2001-2004 Corvette rpm points (see notes). Holden rating periods are taken from handbook and brochure print dates (estimated). Only the 250 kW VT II HSV range is modelled; the Callaway C4B 300 kW GTS, the 255/285 kW HSVs, the VZ Commodore SS and the GM Performance Parts LS1 crate engine (P/N 25534322, 10.25:1, no rating found) are not (see report).

bellhousing.note: GM Gen III/IV LS pattern: the traditional Chevrolet small/big-block bellhousing pattern with the same dowels and 5 of its 6 bolt holes, but the crank flange sits about 0.400 in deeper (Speedway Motors), so older gearboxes need LS-specific bellhousings (T5, TKO/TKX, Muncie) or, for TH350/700R4/Powerglide, a dished or spaced flexplate plus a converter-hub sleeve (the non-LS converter pilot is about 0.350 in shorter). Factory LS1 gearboxes: Tremec (Borg-Warner) T56 6-speed manual and Hydra-Matic 4L60-E automatic (Corvette rear-mounted transaxle versions with a torque tube, F-body/GTO/Holden front-mounted); 4L80E-family automatics bolt up with their 11.5 in converter pattern. Speedway sells one steel LS bellhousing for both the T-56 and TR-6060. LS1 cranks have a 6-bolt flange (8- and 9-bolt flanges began in 2009) and all LS flexplates are 168-tooth, 14 in, internally balanced. Exception within the family: the 1999-2000 LQ4 6.0 truck engine had a long crank flange (not an LS1).

sources.title: OnAllCylinders (Summit Racing), Brian Nutter (Summit product developer, formerly Wiseco piston development), 19 Oct 2017: LS1 5.7L Engine Upgrade Guide
sources.note: 'The stock pistons are a known weak point.' ... 'The excess heat can cause the top piston ring to expand. Under enough heat, it will close the ring gap and the ends will butt together. When they do, a broken ring land can result.' ... 'Broken ring lands can happen with as little as 450 hp in road racing, or 600 hp in drag racing.'

value.note: Road-racing figure; the same sentence gives 600 hp for drag racing.

reportedLimits.context: Summit Racing tech article by a former Wiseco piston developer: ring-land failures on stock pistons from heat-induced ring butting, at as little as 450 hp in sustained road racing or 600 hp in drag racing. Says forged pistons should be high on the upgrade list; no fuel or tune stated.

reportedLimits.context: Stock powdered-metal rods with the 2001-on (LS6-type) bolts, naturally aspirated, to 7,000 rpm (OnAllCylinders/Summit). The 1997-2000 bolts are called a weak point without a figure, so treat early engines as lower.
